title: SMORE: Knowledge Graph Completion and Multi-hop Reasoning in Massive Knowledge Graphs

problem.claim: Knowledge graph reasoning requires both single-hop link prediction and multi-hop logical-query reasoning.

gap.claim: Existing scalable knowledge graph embedding frameworks support single-hop completion but not multi-hop reasoning.

contributions.claim: SMORE is a general framework supporting both single-hop and multi-hop reasoning in knowledge graphs.
SMORE uses bidirectional rejection sampling, asynchronous scheduling, and overlapped CPU/GPU processing to improve scalability and runtime performance.
SMORE supports multi-hop reasoning on a single machine for the 86M-entity, 338M-edge Freebase knowledge graph.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe SMORE as the first general framework for both single-hop and multi-hop reasoning in knowledge graphs and identify bidirectional rejection sampling as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: SMORE performs multi-hop reasoning on Freebase, described as 1,500 times larger than previously considered knowledge graphs.

SMORE achieves a 2.2x throughput increase over prior multi-hop knowledge graph frameworks, uses 2GB of GPU memory for the stated 400-dimensional, 86M-node training setup, and achieves near-linear speed-up with more GPUs.
SMORE has comparable or better runtime performance than state-of-the-art frameworks for single-hop completion in single-GPU and multi-GPU settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Knowledge graphs represent knowledge as entity-relation triples and support important AI systems.
The relevant reasoning tasks are single-hop completion and multi-hop logical-query reasoning, commonly addressed with embeddings.
Existing scalable embedding frameworks do not support multi-hop reasoning.
SMORE combines a general framework with bidirectional rejection sampling and asynchronous CPU/GPU scheduling.
The authors report large-scale Freebase capability, improved throughput and GPU efficiency, near-linear multi-GPU scaling, and competitive single-hop runtime.

source_observation.claim: The reported framework overlaps CPU data sampling, GPU embedding computation, and CPU-GPU I/O.

interpretation.claim: Large-scale training throughput may benefit from coordinating heterogeneous computation and data-movement pipelines.

application.claim: When designing scalable learning systems, examine whether sampling, accelerator computation, and transfers can proceed asynchronously.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this scheduling strategy improves every workload or hardware configuration.

source_observation.claim: The authors report a square-root reduction in the complexity of online training-data generation from bidirectional rejection sampling.

interpretation.claim: Reducing the cost of training-data generation can be central to scaling reasoning models.

application.claim: For scalable graph-learning systems, prioritize the complexity of data generation alongside model computation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide the derivation, assumptions, or conditions for the stated complexity reduction.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, query distributions, baselines, or experimental protocols underlying the runtime comparisons.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, accuracy results, or limitations of the framework.
